notes: 16 cases: 9 positive (should_trigger true) / 7 negative (should_trigger false). By origin: 9 golden (authored), 2 real-trace (byte-verbatim production user turns, BOTH negatives), 5 negative (authored near-misses). THERE ARE ZERO REAL-TRACE POSITIVES AND THAT IS A FINDING, NOT AN OMISSION — see known_gaps.no_real_trace_positive_exists: all 5 measured kg invocations in the transcript corpus were agent-internal compositions, never a human asking for a graph load. kg is a LOAD skill and the runner's workspace is a clean temp dir with no knowledge graph in it, so on a positive the only things this set can assert are that the skill fired and that the run was healthy — see check_selection, which states plainly what each check can and cannot fail on. Every unreachable outcome check was deliberately left off rather than stacked (known_gaps.checks_deliberately_not_used), and one check that WAS stacked (connects_to_active_work on golden-01) has been withdrawn after measurement disproved its rationale (check_selection.connects_to_active_work_withdrawn). Two negatives carry the literal string 'kg' and therefore emit the validator's name-matching WARNING on every run — that is deliberate and is the point of those two cases (known_gaps.deliberate_validator_warnings). Authored prompts are written in the register of this user's real turns (lowercase, dropped apostrophes, comma splices, no em dashes); the two real traces are reproduced byte-for-byte including the 'where does kg skill lives?' agreement error.

execution_contract.advisory: Documentation only — runner.py does not read this object; it is here so the intended contract is reviewable and so drift between intent and CLI flags is visible. Every value below was re-read against runner.py's module constants on 2026-07-28: DEFAULT_TRIALS=3 (runner.py:78), DEFAULT_THRESHOLD=0.80 (:79), DEFAULT_CASE_THRESHOLD=0.60 (:80), DEFAULT_MODEL='haiku' (:81), DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S=300 (:82). execution_contract.workspace: clean temp dir per trial; skill installed at .claude/skills/kg; --setting-sources project; --permission-mode bypassPermissions; --no-session-persistence
execution_contract.negative_semantics: runner.grade_trial:1047-1048 returns FAIL for a should_trigger:false trial whenever transcript.triggered(skill) is true, attaching the check results (`checks=check_dicts`) but NOT reading them. Failed checks only reach a verdict on the non-triggered path, at :1049-1051. So on a negative the checks are additive assertions about what the run did INSTEAD of firing: they can turn a correct non-trigger into a FAIL, and they can never turn an over-trigger into a PASS. The non-trigger assertion is structural and independent of everything in expected_checks.
execution_contract.positive_semantics: Same ordering (see check_ordering). runner.grade_trial:1030-1044 handles should_trigger:true. If the skill did not fire, :1031-1038 returns RECOVERED (when transcript.read_skill_content finds the run answered by reading SKILL.md off disk, :1032-1037) or FAIL (:1038), again attaching the check results without reading them. Failed checks matter only at :1039-1043, once the skill HAS fired. So 'skill_triggered' in a positive's expected_checks is REDUNDANT with the structural assertion — it can never fail a trial that :1038 would not already have failed. It is listed anyway so the case's primary claim is visible in the file instead of living only in the runner's control flow, and no positive here rests on it alone.
execution_contract.check_ordering: READ THIS BEFORE REASONING ABOUT WHAT A CHECK CAN CHANGE. grade_trial runs the checks EARLY and branches LATE. Order in runner.py: is_error short-circuits to ERROR at :1000-1001; the roster/visibility guards follow; `triggered = transcript.triggered(skill)` at :1014; `check_results = checks_mod.run_checks(case.expected_checks, ctx)` at :1026; and only then the should_trigger branch at :1030. So expected_checks are ALWAYS evaluated and always attached to the trial record — including on trials whose verdict ignores them entirely. An earlier revision of this object said the trigger verdict is reached 'BEFORE expected_checks are consulted'; that was wrong about the mechanism, and is corrected in the two entries below. The conclusion it was used to support (checks cannot rescue or cause a trigger verdict) survives, because the branch ignores `failed` on exactly those paths.

verification_log.runner_env_caveat: READ THIS BEFORE ADDING AN OUTCOME CHECK TO A POSITIVE. LiveRunner.run (runner.py:673-684) calls subprocess.run with cwd=<temp workspace> and NO env= argument — re-read 2026-07-28, the call passes only argv, cwd, stdin, capture_output, text and timeout — so the child inherits the parent environment, including HOME. kg's SKILL.md hardcodes absolute paths (`python3 ~/.claude/skills/kg/scripts/kg.py` at SKILL.md:86, `ls -la ~/broomva/docs/knowledge-index.md` at SKILL.md:71) and kg.py resolves its root at scripts/kg.py:96 as `Path(env.get('BROOMVA_ROOT') or (Path.home() / 'broomva'))`, which kg.py:101-106 then lets KG_ROOT / KG_ENTITIES_DIR / KG_CATALOG override per key (an earlier revision cited only the line-96 default; the override chain does not change the conclusion, because the harness sets none of those variables either). On the AUTHOR's machine ~/.claude/skills/kg and ~/broomva/docs/knowledge-index.md both exist, so a positive can incidentally load the real graph from inside the 'clean' temp workspace. That is machine-local luck, not the harness contract. Any check asserted on entities actually being loaded would pass here and fail on any box without ~/broomva — the textbook environmental false-signal. Every case in this set is therefore written to the STATED contract (no knowledge graph present), and no check depends on the graph resolving.

check_selection.advisory: Documentation only — runner.py does not read this object. What each asserted check can ACTUALLY fail on, measured on 2026-07-28 by importing the predicate from scripts/skill_evals/checks.py and running it, not by reading it. A field that says a check discriminates without a demonstration is the same forward-honesty defect as a README describing a withdrawn check as sound.
check_selection.standard: A check earns a place here only if a run that behaves BADLY can fail it and a run that behaves WELL cannot. Eight of the eleven registry ids fail that bar here and are asserted nowhere, on grounds that differ per id and are stated per id in known_gaps.checks_deliberately_not_used — two of them (1) and (3) specifically because they fire on phrasing luck, which measurement confirmed in both directions. Two ids that do not fully meet the bar are nevertheless carried, and both are labelled below rather than dressed up as coverage. Applying that standard in this pass removed one check and made a second uniform.
check_selection.skill_triggered: Asserted on all 9 positives, on no negative. Falsifiable in principle and it is the set's primary claim, but it adds NO failure surface: per execution_contract.positive_semantics the runner already returns FAIL/RECOVERED at runner.py:1031-1038 on the same condition, before the branch that reads check results. It is listed for visibility of the claim, not for coverage. Counting it as an assertion would inflate the apparent rigour of every positive.
check_selection.final_answer_non_empty: Asserted on all 16. THE ONLY CHECK IN THIS SET THAT CAN INDEPENDENTLY CHANGE A VERDICT ON AGENT BEHAVIOUR. check_final_answer_non_empty (checks.py:406-424) fails a final result that is empty, is under 3 words (_MIN_ANSWER_WORDS, checks.py:387), or matches _STUB_RE (checks.py:398-403: 'ok', 'sure', 'done', 'yes', 'got it', 'will do', 'see above', 'n/a', 'tbd', an ellipsis, and similar acknowledgements). A run that fires kg and then says 'Done.' fails it; so does a negative that abstains with 'Got it.' On a positive that triggered it reaches the verdict at runner.py:1039-1043, and on a correct non-trigger at runner.py:1049-1051. It is a low floor and it is not a quality measure, but it is genuinely falsifiable on something the agent chose to do.
check_selection.no_permission_denials: RUN-HEALTH SENTINEL, NOT BEHAVIOURAL COVERAGE. Asserted uniformly on all 16 cases as of this pass; an earlier revision carried it on 11 of 16 with no principle separating the 11 from the 5, which was an inconsistent padding standard and is the defect being fixed. What it does: check_no_permission_denials (checks.py:427-432) reads Transcript.permission_denials, which is whatever the CLI put in the result event's `permission_denials` array (transcript.py:412-416). What that means here: LiveRunner.build_argv (runner.py:648-667) passes `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` (runner.py:661-662), and passes `--disallowedTools` only under the opt-in `--disallow-recovery-tools` flag (runner.py:641, :665-666, default False), which this set's contract does not use. Under that invocation the agent's own choices cannot produce a denial; only a harness or sandbox anomaly can. Measured: all 13 recorded transcripts under tests/skill_evals/fixtures/ carry `"permission_denials": []` and not one carries a non-empty array. So the check CAN fail, but essentially never on anything the skill did. It is here so that a trigger result stays interpretable — a denial would mean the run was constrained, not that the description failed — and it must not be read as evidence about kg's behaviour. It is never the only check on a case: every case also carries final_answer_non_empty, and every negative additionally rests on the structural non-trigger assertion. REMOVED IN THIS PASS: two per-case justifications claiming it was carried 'for a stated reason rather than as filler' because certain prompts were 'most likely to make the run shell out to the loader script with a flag'. That was unverifiable, it presented a run-health sentinel as behavioural coverage, and its own count was wrong — the check sat on four positives, not the three the note claimed.
check_selection.connects_to_active_work_withdrawn: WITHDRAWN from golden-01 in this pass. The prior rationale claimed it 'is a real discriminator here and not a freebie: an agent that returns a neutral essay on distributed leases, never tying it to the helper the user says exists in two places, fails it.' That is FALSE. Measurement showed it is not merely a freebie but INVERTED on this case. The predicate is a bare regex search over the agent's output text: _ACTIVE_WORK_RE (checks.py:451-456) = `\b(our |we already|we're building|we are building|existing |current(?:ly)? |in (?:our|the) (?:stack|repo|workspace)|relates to|overlaps with|compared? (?:to|with) (?:our|the existing)|already have|BRO-\d+|your (?:stack|repo|work|harness))`, IGNORECASE|MULTILINE. Run against constructed answers on 2026-07-28: (a) 5 of 6 NEUTRAL ESSAYS that never mention the user's helper PASS — 'In our field, leases are usually paired with fencing tokens' hits 'our ', 'Leases are currently the standard approach to bounded mutual exclusion' hits 'currently ', 'The existing literature distinguishes fencing tokens from bare TTLs' hits 'existing '. That is exactly the failure mode the rationale said it catches. (b) 3 of 3 answers that DO tie back to the user's helper FAIL — 'Nothing on disk covers the duplicated lease helper you described' matches no alternative, because the regex has no general arm for second-person reference to the user's own artifact ('your (?:stack|repo|work|harness)' is a closed four-word list). (c) Worst, 4 of 4 honest answers under THIS SET'S OWN stated contract (no knowledge graph in the temp workspace) FAIL — 'I could not find a knowledge catalog in this workspace, so there is nothing recorded to surface on leases or idempotency' matches nothing. So on golden-01 the check false-passes the behaviour it was cited against and false-fails the correct behaviour, which on a 3-trial / 0.6-threshold case makes it a false-fail generator. Independently reproduced: the reviewer's own probe, 'I am currently unable to find any feature flags in this directory, so I created a fresh project', hits 'currently ' and PASSES. Dropped on exactly the ground this file already used to reject mentions_source_verification (known_gaps.checks_deliberately_not_used item 1) — keeping one while rejecting the other was an inconsistent standard. Consequence, stated plainly: NO check in this set now claims to grade kg's OUTPUT at all (known_gaps.positives_assert_triggering_plus_run_health_only).

known_gaps.no_real_trace_positive_exists: The corpus contains no human turn that asked kg to load anything. All 5 measured invocations are agent-internal (3 nested inside /checkit, 1 inside a loop file, 1 under 'im testing skills and tools, please run some') — see verification_log.kg_invocation_census. The three /checkit turns were considered and REJECTED as kg cases on two independent grounds: they measure checkit's routing, not kg's, and checkit is not installed in kg's eval workspace, so '/checkit <url>' would arrive as an unknown slash command and the case would grade the harness. The moltbook loop turn names a filesystem path that does not exist in a temp workspace. 'im testing skills and tools, please run some' has no ground-truth label — it asks for arbitrary skills to fire, so neither true nor false is defensible; it also arrives wrapped in a Conductor <system_instruction> preamble that would have to be stripped or carried, and neither choice is faithful. All 9 positives are therefore AUTHORED. This is stated rather than papered over by relabelling a golden as real-trace.
known_gaps.checks_deliberately_not_used: CHECK_REGISTRY holds 11 ids (re-enumerated by import 2026-07-28: connects_to_active_work, documents_finding, final_answer_non_empty, ingests_full_artifact_not_metadata, mentions_source_verification, no_clarifying_question_bounced_back, no_permission_denials, produces_ranked_next_steps, skill_triggered, traverses_to_primitives, walks_repo_tree_and_canonical_files). This set asserts 3. The other 8 are asserted NOWHERE here, each for a stated reason. (1) mentions_source_verification — kg's Phase 1 is literally headed '### Phase 1 — Verify catalog freshness' (SKILL.md:66), so the vocabulary is tempting, but _VERIFY_RE (checks.py:439-443) wants 'verif*', 'could not confirm/verify', 'unverified', 'citation', 'cited'. Measured: an honest graph-less answer phrased 'I could not find the catalog' matches NONE of those arms, while the same answer phrased 'I could not verify that the catalog exists' hits 'could not verify'. Identical behaviour, opposite verdicts — a coin flip on wording, and a coin flip on a 3-trial / 0.6-threshold case is a false-fail generator. (2) produces_ranked_next_steps — needs >=2 enumerated items AND next-step language (checks.py:602-612); kg's documented Phase-3 'reading frontier' use would produce that against a real graph, but with no graph loaded the honest answer is one sentence about the missing catalog. (3) documents_finding — kg is a READ skill; a run that writes a file has misread the ask. Worse, measured: _DOCUMENT_RE (checks.py:458-462) false-PASSES on the sentence 'I could not find any documented entities', hitting the span 'documented entities' — a write-verb from its own alternation followed by 'entities' inside the 80-character window — so it grades string luck in both directions. (4) traverses_to_primitives — reachable only on the subset of prompts that ask how something works, and only if the graph resolves. (5) walks_repo_tree_and_canonical_files — kg walks a catalog, not a repo tree; the check is shaped for artifact ingestion. (6) ingests_full_artifact_not_metadata — scopes tool evidence to an artifact named in the prompt (checks.py:300-323 via _case_artifact_tokens); no prompt here names one (verification_log.external_urls), so _artifact_tokens returns empty, _hits_artifact is vacuously true, and ANY read or fetch would satisfy it. That is the tool-name vacuity checks.py's own design rule 3 exists to reject. (7) no_clarifying_question_bounced_back — a real and well-built predicate, but it grades a conversational failure mode kg's description does not own; it belongs to skills whose SKILL.md prescribes the answer-then-offer shape, and asserting it here would grade the base model's manners, not the routing decision. (8) completed_without_error — see the next entry; it is no longer in the registry at all. Fewer checks that can actually fail beat more checks that fail for reasons other than the skill.
known_gaps.positives_assert_triggering_plus_run_hea: Every positive here asserts exactly three ids: skill_triggered (redundant-by-design, see execution_contract.positive_semantics), final_answer_non_empty, and no_permission_denials (a run-health sentinel, see check_selection.no_permission_denials). Nothing else. As of this pass NO case asserts connects_to_active_work — it was withdrawn from golden-01 after measurement showed it inverted on that case (check_selection.connects_to_active_work_withdrawn) — so the honest summary is that on a positive this set grades kg's TRIGGERING deterministically and its OUTPUT not at all beyond a 3-word floor. That is thinner than checkit's positives, and the reason is structural, not laziness: checkit's outcome checks grade what an INGEST produced, while kg's product is context loaded into the agent's window, and the registry has no check that can see it. The two ids that would make a kg positive substantive — something like `loaded_entities_into_context` (the answer names entity slugs / types / a catalog it actually read) and `cited_entity_paths` (the answer attributes claims back to research/entities/<type>/<slug>.md, which is exactly what kg's bordered output format is designed to make easy) — do not exist. They are NOT referenced anywhere here, because an unknown id is a hard PromptSetError that would make the whole file unloadable. Stated plainly so nobody reads a green suite as evidence that kg loads well.
known_gaps.deliberate_validator_warnings: real-trace-01 and real-trace-02 both contain the literal string 'kg', so `runner.py --validate-only` prints "WARNING case '<id>': prompt contains the literal skill name 'kg' — this measures name-matching, not description-matching" for each (runner.py:486). Re-confirmed 2026-07-28: exactly two warnings, and exit code 0. The warning is CORRECT about what it detects and WRONG to worry about here, for two reasons. First, both cases are NEGATIVES: a prompt that names the skill and must not fire it is the sharpest possible test of name-matching — a router that fires on its own name fails exactly these two. Second, both prompts are byte-verbatim production turns; paraphrasing them to silence the warning would destroy the provenance that makes them worth carrying. No AUTHORED prompt in this set contains 'kg' as a substring — re-checked programmatically 2026-07-28 with a case-insensitive scan of all 16 prompts, which returns hits on the two real traces and on nothing else, including the words that could hide it such as 'background' and 'workgroup'.
known_gaps.no_negative_on_the_long_form_ingest_axis: kg's SKILL.md 'When NOT to use' also lists long-form content ingestion (use Knowledge ingest). No negative covers it. Omitted deliberately: a faithful instantiation is 'here is a 50-page document, read it and store it', which in a temp workspace either needs a file that does not exist (environmental) or needs 50 pages pasted into the prompt (a token bomb that would grade the context window). The write axis is already covered twice, and Knowledge ingest is a write. Reopen if the harness gains a fixture-file seam.

The internal-substrate signal is 'weve written down' plus 'something we settled', i.e. prior recorded decisions, which is exactly the semantic ('what do we know') half of the split SKILL.md draws against ContextSearch's episodic half. negative-02 is the matched opposite on that axis. WHAT THIS CASE NO LONGER CLAIMS: an earlier revision asserted connects_to_active_work here and called it 'a real discriminator here and not a freebie: an agent that returns a neutral essay on distributed leases, never tying it to the helper the user says exists in two places, fails it.' 'have we captured anything on' is a paraphrase of the description's 'find entities about' / 'what do we know about' without reusing either string. 'dump ... into context so i can reason over them' restates the skill's own architectural claim (surface bodies as one block; the agent is the query engine) without borrowing its vocabulary. An earlier revision justified no_permission_denials here by claiming this was 'one of the three prompts most likely to make the run shell out to the loader script with a flag'; that was an unverified guess presented as a reason, and the count was wrong besides. cases.prompt: start me at write-reachability-underdetermines-grounding and walk out one hop. i want that page plus whatever it links to, all in one block.
cases.workspace_requires: none, and this is load-bearing for the case. The slug is REAL (verification_log.entity_slug records the file and its SIX-entry related: block, re-counted on disk 2026-07-28, which is what makes 'one hop' a meaningful ask rather than decoration), but the case does not require it to resolve at run time — an honest 'that slug is not in the catalog I can see' is still a correct kg run, because what is being graded is whether the traversal ask routes here.
cases.rationale: The positive that sits deliberately ON the boundary with the skill's own 'Single-entity reads when you already know the slug — just use Read directly' exclusion (SKILL.md:176). A bare 'open that page' would be a plain Read and would belong on the negative side; 'plus whatever it links to' is graph 1-hop expansion, which Read cannot perform without first resolving edges. ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED 2026-07-28: an earlier revision credited 'the structural advantage flat-document search (BM25, vector) structurally cannot offer' to the description. That phrase is SKILL.md:48-49, in the body, which the router never reads. What the DESCRIPTION actually carries — and therefore what this case can legitimately test routing against — is '--expand 1 (graph 1-hop — also load related: neighbours of top hits, capped at --n extra, total ≤ 2x--n)'. The case tests whether the boundary is read at the right place, not whether a slug was recognised. cases.prompt:
ive got the page right here so no need to go pull anything. does the claim line and the body actually say the same thing, or am i reading two different statements into one page?

---
slug: verification-edge-classification
type: concept
status: candidate
tags: [verification, grounding, ci]
claim: A verification edge is anchored only when the actor being verified cannot write to the signals producer.
related: [self-referential-verification, grounding-ratio, review-gate]
---

An edge is classified anchored, self-referential, or unknown. The classifier asks one question: can the actor under test write to the thing that produces the signal? Everything else, who wrote the test, how green CI is, how many assertions ran, is downstream of that and cannot substitute for it.

The unknown bucket is not a failure state. It is the queue that gets turned into probes.
cases.artifact: an entity page carried INLINE in the prompt. This is authored illustrative content, not a citation: no file at this slug is claimed to exist and none is read. It is shaped like a catalog entry (slug / type / status / tags / claim / related) precisely so that it functions as bait.
cases.workspace_requires: none — the artifact IS the prompt. No path, no URL, no graph.
cases.rationale: AXIS: there is nothing to ROUTE. kg's job is the routing step — decide which of the graph's bodies to put in context (823 entity files under research/entities/ as counted on 2026-07-28; SKILL.md:15 still says '~250 entities', which is the skill's own stale figure and not something this eval set asserts) — and the one body in question is already in context, pasted whole. Every token needed to answer sits in the prompt. This is the sharpest near-miss in the set because the surface similarity is maximal: the pasted block is catalog frontmatter, and three of its keys (slug, tags, claim) are literally among the tier-1 signals the description names — 'slug + tags + claim + links + sources match against docs/knowledge-index.md' — with the fourth, `related`, being the substrate form of that clause's `links`. (An earlier revision listed `related` itself as a named tier-1 signal; it is not, and the wording is corrected.) A careless reader sees graph frontmatter and reaches for the graph loader. The question is deliberately scoped INSIDE the pasted text — does the claim line agree with the body — so that loading the three named neighbours would not help; had the question been 'is the related list still right', loading them would arguably be correct and the label would be arguable. Single axis, and the label does not depend on judgement about the neighbours.

cases.prompt: what did we land on for the lease ttl in the end? we went round on it in a session a couple of weeks back, 30 seconds versus 5 minutes, and i want the reasoning we actually used that day rather than a fresh opinion.
cases.workspace_requires: none. Both candidate values are supplied inline, so the turn is answerable-as-far-as-it-goes without session history: the correct move is to say that a past session's deliberation is not something this skill retrieves, and route or reason accordingly.
cases.rationale: AXIS: episodic versus semantic. SKILL.md states the split in its own words at SKILL.md:166 — '**ContextSearch** is upstream (PAI session retrieval) — call it for "what did we do" questions; call this skill for "what do we know" questions' — and the description's NOT FOR opens with 'PAI session retrieval (use ContextSearch)'. This prompt is anchored hard on the episodic side by 'in a session', 'that day', and 'the reasoning we actually used', which asks for a deliberation as it happened rather than a settled claim. It is a genuine near-miss because 'what did we land on' is one lexical step from the USE WHEN entry 'what do we know about', and because a decision CAN eventually become an entity, which is the ambiguity a careless router collapses. Deliberately not lifted from the exclusion list: the phrase 'PAI session retrieval' appears nowhere in the prompt, and recognising the case requires knowing what makes a question about a past conversation different from a question about recorded knowledge. golden-01 is the paired positive on this axis — it asks for what was settled, not for how the settling went.

cases.prompt: find me the primary sources people keep citing for speculative decoding throughput numbers. papers not blog posts, three or four is plenty. ill file the good ones later.
cases.workspace_requires: none beyond network access. The prompt bounds the ask to three or four sources. An earlier revision added 'so the run cannot balloon past the timeout'; that causal claim is deleted rather than softened, because nothing in this session measured run time against the 300s timeout.
cases.rationale: AXIS: external versus internal substrate. The description's NOT FOR names 'web research (use Research)'. Everything asked for is outside the graph — 'primary sources people keep citing' is by definition not our own pages. The bait is deliberate and layered: the shape is identical to a topical load ('find me ... on <topic>'), the verb 'find' echoes the USE WHEN entry 'find entities about', and the trailing 'ill file the good ones later' plants the knowledge graph in the frame without making it the object of the request. golden-02 is the matched opposite — same 'get me sources on a topic' shape, internal rather than external — so the pair isolates the discriminating variable to WHERE the knowledge lives rather than to any surface feature of the phrasing.

cases.prompt: the entity catalog is a couple of days stale, two pages i added yesterday arent showing up in it at all. rebuild it before we do anything else.
cases.workspace_requires: none. The premise mentions pages added yesterday, but nothing needs to be read: the ask is to regenerate, and the correct answer in a workspace with no catalog is to say what regeneration would take and that it is not this skill's job.
cases.rationale: AXIS: rebuild the routing projection versus use it. SKILL.md's own 'When NOT to use' ends at SKILL.md:177 with '**Catalog generation** — that's `bookkeeping index`, not this skill' (re-checked 2026-07-28: it is the last bullet of that section), and this instantiates it in the user's phrasing without borrowing the words 'catalog generation' or 'bookkeeping index'. It is the subtlest bait here because the catalog is not an unrelated object — it is kg's OWN input, kg's Phase 1 is a freshness check on exactly this file ('### Phase 1 — Verify catalog freshness', SKILL.md:66), and the skill even tells the agent to regenerate a stale one before loading (SKILL.md:181). The distinction the case turns on is that Phase 1 makes staleness a PRECONDITION kg checks, while this turn makes regeneration the WHOLE deliverable ('before we do anything else'), and there is no topic to load afterwards. A router that keys on the noun 'entity catalog' fires; one that reads the verb does not.

cases.prompt: draft me an entity page for the pattern where fixing a defect in an edge dense file opens the next one at an adjacent edge. frontmatter with a claim, tags and related, then the body. i already know what goes in it, ill drop the file in myself.
cases.workspace_requires: none — no path is named and no file is written; the user says they will place it themselves, which removes the filesystem dependency the natural version of this ask would carry.
cases.rationale: AXIS: producing a NEW node versus retrieving existing ones — the same write axis as real-trace-01, carried a second time on purpose and for a stated reason. real-trace-01 is the production instance and is terse to the point of being under-contextualized; this one is the fully-specified authored instance, so the pair separates 'the skill correctly ignores a write' from 'the skill correctly ignores an ambiguous fragment'. The near-miss is real: the prompt is thick with catalog vocabulary (entity page, frontmatter, claim, tags, related) and the tempting rationalisation is that neighbours should be loaded before authoring. The clause that closes that door is 'i already know what goes in it' — there is no gap for a load to fill, and the description's NOT FOR routes entity writes to direct Read+Edit+commit. Deliberately NOT the exclusion clause restated: nothing in the prompt says 'write' or 'edit' or names an operation type, so recognising it means reading what a draft request is.
